notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-d67081 (issue #1412). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance. Both recorded hashes match byte for byte: the published offprint from Calegari's research page, 4d27afab...7150290 (12 pp.), and the arXiv v3 PDF, abfa9eac...84769684. I also took the v3 e-print (a single WeightZeroPublished.tex with its .bbl) and every quotation below was checked in it.

Numbering and coverage. The class numbers theorems, corollaries, lemmas, definitions and remarks off the subsection counter, so plain subsection headings advance it too, while the introduction's Problem/Theorem environments run on a separate counter printed with \Alph. Simulating that gives Problems A and C and Theorem B in the introduction, and 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 as the numbered statements, with 1.3 and 2.3 being headings - which is exactly the numbering the extraction's locators use. Every numbered statement is covered, and Theorem B and Problem C are covered by name. Problem A is not a separate item, which is right: it asserts nothing, and it is the question Theorem B answers. The locator numbers that match nothing in the paper (1.4, 1.6, 4.2, 7.1) are citations into the cited papers carried inside the locators.

Statuses. The three library items check out at pinned Mathlib 082e2d3, read in the source at that commit: ModularForm.levelOne_weight_two_rank_zero and ModularForm.dimension_level_one and ModularForm.rank_eq_one_add_rank_cuspForm in NumberTheory/ModularForms/LevelOne/DimensionFormula.lean (lines 245, 250, 171, inside namespace ModularForm), cyclotomicCharacter and modularCyclotomicCharacter in NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean (307, 212), ModularForm.discriminant and CuspForm.discriminant in NumberTheory/ModularForms/Discriminant.lean (52, 239, each inside its namespace) and ModularForm.E4/E6 in EisensteinSeries/Basic.lean (51, 54). The 13 planned items cite 20 layers between them and the routes; all 20 exist in data/atlas.json.

Routes. Two Part IIs and eight source routes, all accepted; see the route verdicts. Both Part II titles reproduce their parents' titles verbatim, and neither opens a rival roadmap: PolarizedAutomorphyLifting is already proposed with the same parent and the same title by PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 and PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23, and PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 already refers to LevelOneCuspidalCohomologyGLn by name.

Mistakes in the paper. All 8 were checked at their locators and all 8 are confirmed; nothing was corrected in place. Four were settled at the cited sources, which is what this paper's findings turn on: Thorne's own section 10 shows 10.1 is the fixed-component theorem and 10.2 the ordinary one, and BLGGT introduce their Theorem 2.4.2 as 'Theorem 10.2 of [Tho12]' (E2); BLGGT's Theorem 2.1.1(4) carries the Iwahori hypothesis and their own following paragraph says they quote Caraiani only in that case (E6); Bellovin-Gee's Definition 4.2.1 requires dim H^0 = dim G - dim B at every infinite place, which an even multiplier alone does not give (E5); and Guralnick-Herzig-Tiep cite Thorne's 2-adic paper as 'Corollary 7.3' for precisely the statement the proof needs (E3). Two were settled by computation: with theta rather than theta' the induced representation has multiplier eps^(3-k-p) and repeated Hodge-Tate weights, against the required eps^(1-(k-1)p) and {0,...,(k-1)p-1} - at p = 79, k = 38 that is eps^(-114) against eps^(-2922) (E4); and the Citro-Ghitza table gives 151: C[52] with (150,51) = 3, so 151 fails hypothesis (2) of Theorem 2.1, while 107: C[26], 139: C[20], 173: C[68], 179: C[30], 191: C[30] and 193: C[48] all have gcd 1 - the corrected list, including the two primes the entry adds (E7). The paper's other list is untouched and right, since 151: N[60] has (59,152) = 1.

One limit of this review, recorded rather than glossed: Thorne's Math. Z. 2017 paper is not on arXiv and no author copy was reachable from here, so E3 rests on Guralnick-Herzig-Tiep's citation of the same paper rather than on my own reading of its section 7.

Verdict: accept.
